FOREWORD
This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Sectional Cornmi tree had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Diflubcnzuron acts by interfering with the deposition of chitin, one of the main components of the insect cuticle.
Diflubenzuron, technical is employed in the preparation of insecticidal formulations.

Diflubenzuron is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO) for I -- (4-chlorophcnyl) -- 3-(2, 6-difluorobenzoyl) lCl urea. The empirical and structural formulae and molecular mass of diflubenzuron are given below:

DETF:RMINATION OF DIFLUBENZURON CONTENT A-I PRINCIPLE
Diflubenzuron in the sample is dissolved in dioxane by heating and scpara.ted by means ,?f liquid l.:hromatography. DJ11ubenzuron IS detected by measuring t he absorption. at 2~4 nm and quanr it at ivcly cst imar ed by using dibutyl phthalate as the internal standard.

A-4.3 Preparation of Standard Solution
Weigh accurately 100 mg reference standard diflubcnzuro n into a tOO-mt volumetric flask, add about 50 ml of dioxane and place it on a steam-bath for 30 minutes. Remove, cool, filter through G, sintered crucible and make up the volume with dioxane by repeated rinsing. A-4.4 Preparation of Sample Solution Liquid Chromatograph Weigh accurately a quantity of sample to contain about 100 mg diflubenzuron technical and proceed as described in A-4.3. A-4.5 Estimation A-4.5.1 Mix reference standard and internal sta ndard solution in I: I (v/v) accurately using a pipette. Follow the same procedure for sample solution.
